paragraphs.text: Fictional variants of Earth are settings in multiple Universes Beyond franchises. In Doctor Who , Earth is a non-canon plane subtype featured on several Planechase cards.
Earth is not a part of the Multiverse , or the lore of Magic more generally.

Earth is not considered to be part of either the Magic: The Gathering Multiverse or the Un-iverse . This is because R&D doesn't want to tell stories about planeswalkers visiting Earth or being from Earth. The setting of Portal Three Kingdoms closely resembles historic Earth, and the set draws heavily on the historical novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms . Statements by members of R&D explain this in differing ways, either placing the set on an unnamed plane, or comparing Portal Three Kingdoms to Universes Beyond and setting it outside of the Multiverse entirely.

Gavin Verhey used Earth as a non-canon plane for Wizards of the Coast in the Unknown Event at MagicCon Minneapolis 2023 . Amsterdam , Atlanta , Chicago and Las Vegas have also been playtest card planar types at various Unknown Events . Playtest cards are not canonical.

Outside of Universes Beyond and Portal Three Kingdoms , Earth and locations on Earth are visible in the art of a small number of cards, including the Heroes of the Realm celebration card Euroakus , Presence of the Master , and the basic lands of the Asia-Pacific Land Program and European Land Program .
Earth is an extremely common setting for fiction, and will certainly be a setting in future Universes Beyond sets. On a Universes Beyond version of the Rabiah Scale , Earth is a 1.

In Doctor Who , Earth is also known as Sol III (or Sol 3), mostly by extraterrestrial cultures. In addition to humans, Doctor Who' s Earth is also home to a second native sapient species, the Silurians . Earth is favored by The Doctor.
